Aachal Maniyar Published 10 Nov 2026, 06:09 PM IST Prefer Livemint on Google Harmeet Singh strikes against his old NPL side ( NPL/X ) AI Quick Read Harmeet Singh turned the screw on his former team as Janakpur Bolts restricted Sudurpaschim Royals to 120 for 9 in 20 overs in the 21st match of the Nepal Premier League at the Tribhuvan University International Cricket Ground in Kirtipur. The India 2012 Under-19 World Cup winner, now captaining the Bolts, returned figures of 4 for 17 from his full quota of four overs. The Royals had won the toss and elected to bat, leaving Janakpur a target of 121. Who is Harmeet Singh? Harmeet Singh came through the ranks as a left-arm spinner and was part of the India side that lifted the 2012 Under-19 World Cup. Rajasthan Royals signed him the following year. He has since represented the United States. Janakpur named him captain for the league’s third season in August. According to Khabarhub, he scored 28 runs and took eight wickets in five matches for Sudurpaschim Royals in the first NPL season. In the second season he made 133 runs in nine matches at a strike rate of more than 166, and took 12 wickets at an economy of 6.18. Those numbers made him a useful all-round contributor during Sudurpaschim’s two runs to the final. Now he is trying to plot their downfall. Also Read | T20 World Cup: Monank Patel to Harmeet Singh: Indian-origin players in US team Sudurpaschim’s innings summary Brandon McMullen top-scored with 33 off 23 balls, striking two fours and two sixes, before Harry Tector bowled him. Tector finished with 1 for 9 from four overs. Saif Zaib made 10 before Rahul Yadav bowled him, while Binod Bhandari was run out by Lalit Rajbanshi for 10. Ishan Pandey was bowled by Harmeet for 3 off 8, and captain Dipendra Singh Airee lasted only three balls before Aaditya Mahata caught him off his own bowling for 1. Also Read | Canadian Yuvraj Samra lights up NPL 2026 with first hundred of the season Aarif Sheikh scored 11 off 16 before Abhisekh Tiwari had him caught behind by Anil Sah. Scott Kuggeleijn (6), Anil Kharel (4) and Hemant Dhami (0) all fell to Harmeet, whose four wickets came at a cost of just 17 runs. Tharindu Ratnayake remained unbeaten on 27 off 28 balls with one four and two sixes, and Abinash Bohara finished on 2 not out. Extras added 13 as the total closed at 120 for 9 What is at stake Before the match, Sudurpaschim stood third in the table with six points from five games, while Janakpur were fifth with four points from five. The two sides had met four times in previous editions of the NPL , with Sudurpaschim winning three and Janakpur one. Harmeet’s 4 for 17 has given the Bolts a clear opening to alter that record and stay in the knockout race.
